sentences.text: Procaimanoidea was a small alligatorid featuring slightly heterodont dentition, meaning its teeth varied in shape, with the last four on each jaw side having blunt tips.
The genus was named in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore after he had already passed away.
Its description relies on fossil USNM 15996, which preserves a nearly complete skull and a partial left hind leg.
The type species P. utahensis was found in the middle Eocene Uintan formation of Utah.
The species P. kayi was originally named in 1941 by C.C. Mook from early Eocene remains in Wyoming before being reassigned to Procaimanoidea by Wassersug and Hecht in 1967.
Recent studies consistently classify Procaimanoidea within the subfamily Alligatorinae, though its exact position within the group remains disputed.
The fossil record for Procaimanoidea spans from the Maastrichtian to the Bartonian stages, between 72.2 and 39.7 million years ago.
